messages:
Maya: Quick proposal — we need to tighten the /rerank contract before the Dedicated rollout. Current ambiguity around score format is causing mismatch in dashboards and canaries.

Ravi: Agree. We see both raw logits and normalized 0..1 floats coming back depending on model variant. Hard to aggregate telemetry. :face_with_raised_eyebrow: 

Lucas: Are we able to force model-side normalization at inference? Some open models don't expose a sigmoid layer easily.

Maya: Two parts: 1) API contract (what we accept/return) 2) routing policy (which model variant we pick for production vs canary). I want the API to require a score object with a format tag. Example: {score:{value:0.123, type: "prob"}} or {score:{value:2.31, type:"logit"}}.

Jing: That helps, yes. But adding a "type" breaks older clients. Are we doing a breaking change or a backwards-compatible extension?

Maya: Backwards-compatible. If type missing, we assume legacy "unknown" and map to legacy pipelines. We should emit a deprecation header for 2 months.

Ravi: Telemetry-wise we need a canonical field for aggregation. Suggest we add normalized_score in the response computed by the platform when type=="logit" or unknown (if we can estimate). That way dashboards and alerts can use a single metric.

Lucas: Compute-normalized at platform sounds expensive for large batch reranks (hundreds of items). How would we do it?

Maya: Two options: A) Platform computes a per-request softmax if model returns logits. B) Model-side adds a normalized_score. B preferred for latency, but we can't require it yet. We'll implement A as fallback but optimize: approximate softmax via max-shift + single pass; parallel on GPU worker.

Jing: Need limits spelled out: max_items_per_request, max_candidates_for_softmax, and response size quotas. Ops team said 512 items is already stressed on some instances.

Ravi: Proposal: limit to 200 items for the standard tier, 1024 for Dedicated high-throughput with billed batch pricing. Platform will return HTTP 413 if exceeded. Also include a response header X-Rerank-Items-Allowed and X-Rerank-Items-Used.

Lucas: Can we add a routing policy: requests with items>200 route to batch pool (higher throughput, higher latency SLA), items<=200 go to low-latency pool. That lets interactive UX stay snappy.

Maya: Exactly. And routing should consider model affinity: if client pins model:alpha-v2 and that model is only on batch pool, we should either reject with 409 or allow with warning header and route to batch. Thoughts?

Jing: Prefer explicit reject (409) for pinned models if not available in the requested tier. Otherwise we silently degrade. But for self-serve, a warning header that we will route to batch might be ok for some customers. Need console UX to show pin->availability.

Ravi: For rollouts/canaries we need weighted routing and score compatibility checks. If canary returns a different score type, we should block canary rollout for metrics pipeline until translation is configured. Add a preflight check that validates response shape and emits sample telemetry.

Maya: Good. I'll draft API spec: - Response includes 'scores' array of objects: {value: string|number, type: string, normalized: number?} - Headers: X-Rerank-Items-Allowed, X-Rerank-Items-Used, X-Rerank-Score-Contract-Version - Error codes: 409 (model affinity conflict), 413 (items too large), 422 (invalid score type) - Deprecation header: X-Rerank-Legacy-Mode until 2 months from rollout.

Lucas: For internal telemetry, add tag 'score_type' and 'normalized_present' to the request trace. That makes dashboards filterable.

Jing: Console UX: show per-route default routing policy, and a toggle for "enforce score contract" (fail canary if mismatch). Otherwise show warnings. Also an indicator for "computed_normalized_score_count" in the cost breakdown.

Ravi: One more: quota accounting. For batch requests we should bill per-candidate token and for low-latency per-response token. Add quota metrics: rerank_items_count, rerank_normalizations_count (for when platform computes softmax).

Maya: OK next steps: I will open an RFC with concrete schema and examples, and a migration plan (headers + deprecation + console flag). @Ravi please add telemetry names. @Lucas can you prototype the softmax fallback on GPU worker? @Jing can you mock a console wireframe for the enforcement toggle?

Ravi: On it.

Lucas: I'll hack a perf test, aim to bench 200 vs 512 items.

Jing: Wireframes later today.

infra-bot: deploy.dag triggered: integration tests for rerank-schema-checks queued (job id: 4238).

Maya: Great. We'll sync in the RFC thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
